Anya (Product): quick sync — we need a decision for embeddings v1 endpoint: batching limits, supported dims, default model, response schema. Major asks: a legaltech customer needs 4096 dims and ~1k vector batches; a mobile partner wants 768 dims + compressed payloads. Launch criteria: support 3 dims (small/medium/large), docs + SDK examples, sensible defaults. Thoughts?
Sam (Eng-Platform): constraints from infra: 4096 dims + large batches blow GPU memory for hosted. Perf tests show 1536x512 ~= safe sweet spot on our p3-like setup. Propose default = 1536, support 768 and 3072 as options. 4096 behind feature-flag / Dedicated only. Also suggest per-tenant max_batch config.
Jia (Eng-ML): model choices + tradeoffs: redwood-embed-1 (1536) = best throughput/quality. We have an experimental redwood-embed-4k but it's 2-3x slower and uses ~2x memory. For accuracy-sensitive customers we can offer 4k in Dedicated. We can also provide auto-quantized int8 representations to reduce memory/cost; small drop in recall.
Matt (DevEx): SDK + schema note: prefer keeping response shape consistent with other endpoints. Suggest: 
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-1",
  "data": [
    {"id": "0","embedding": [0.001, -0.23, ...], "dimension": 1536}
  ],
  "encoding": "float32"
}
```
If we add compressed/int8 base64, include "encoding": "int8-base64" and "original_dimension" meta to be explicit. This avoids breaking clients.
Leo (SRE): ops perspective: batch limit 1024 is risky for hosted during spikes => OOMs and longer GC. Recommend defaults: hosted max_batch = 256, soft fail at 512 with guidance to reduce; Dedicated customers can request higher limits up to 1024 in contract. Also require autoscale ramp and fallback to smaller model (1536) when load is high.
Anya (Product): ok framing — for MVP we should minimize risk. Proposed MVP scope: support dims [768,1536,3072], hosted default 1536, hosted batch limit 256 (max 512), 4096 behind feature-flag for Dedicated. No compressed/int8 in MVP (post-MVP). Docs + SDK examples required. Agree?
Jia (Eng-ML): agree with MVP but swap 3072 -> 4096 as the "large" option behind flag? tradeoff: 3072 gives most of the accuracy uplift of 4k but less memory. We ran evals showing 3072 hits ~0.92 of 4k on our benchmarks. I can surface those numbers. Suggest MVP large=3072, keep 4k experimental.
Sam (Eng-Platform): action items:
- Sam: implement per-tenant batch caps + request validation (hosted default 256, max param 512)
- Jia: provide perf/quality table for 768/1536/3072/4096 and recommended model mapping
- Matt: SDK schema + migration guide (include encoding flag examples)
- Anya: finalize customer comms & launch criteria
ETA: plan to have MVP PRs by next sprint.
Anya (Product): prioritization: we have one enterprise customer willing to pay for Dedicated 4k — block rollout behind contract. For broad GA, aim for 768/1536/3072 with stable SDK and docs. Compression/int8 + bandwidth-optimized payloads = backlog.
Sam (Eng-Platform): quick note on response format — please keep "data" array rather than top-level "embeddings" to allow per-id metadata and multiple models in a single response later. Also include a top-level "usage" object with token counts and cost_estimate for transparency.
Matt (DevEx): +1 to usage/cost metadata. I'll draft examples and a migration section for existing customers who expect a flat array.
Leo (SRE): I'll add tests for OOM scenarios and a canary plan: rollout hosted with traffic cap + circuit-breaker to auto-fail to 1536 if memory pressure spikes.
Anya (Product): decision recap: MVP dims = 768/1536/3072; hosted default 1536; hosted batch default 256, hard cap 512; 4096 for Dedicated/feature-flag only; compressed/int8 deferred. Owners assigned above. Thanks all — I'll update the roadmap ticket and add launch checklist. :thumbsup:
